greeting.text: Alder Pyke is at the far end with his chain in a canvas bag at his feet and a half-pint he has made last since noon. He sees you and does not pretend not to. "Two benches back," he says. "Four days. I thought you'd turn round once. You didn't." He moves the bag so you can sit. "Nobody up the valley will hire a chainman who reads the work out. I'm not complaining. I'd do it again. I'd just like to be paid for something."

interjections.text: Aldric sits down next to him and for a while that is all he does.

greeting.text: "Moss at the yard," Pyke says. "He wants a character. You've seen me work." He looks at his half-pint. "Or don't. I'll not hold it against you either way. I've held enough."

choices.label: Here's sixty for Tull's boat. Go home. Rivermark owes you.

greeting.text: "Monday," Pyke says. "The Lenning. Never heard of it." He hefts the bag. "Chain's chain. It doesn't care whose. That's always been the trouble with it."
"The fifth," Pyke says, with the sixty in his fist. "I'll sit on the granary steps. Somebody'll need a thing measured."
Pyke's bench is empty except for a ring where his pint stood.

the_ask.text: "There's work," he says. "Only one kind on this river. The house's." He laughs, once, without much in it. "Moss at the yard hires chain for a survey going up somebody else's valley. He wants a character from somebody who's seen me work. That's you." He looks at you straight. "I know what I'm asking. I'm asking it anyway. I'm forty-eight, and chain is what I know."

choices.label: Here's sixty for Tull's boat. Go home. Rivermark owes you.

home.text: He looks at the coins for a long time before he takes them. "Owes," he says. "That's a word you could read out on some steps." He puts them in his coat. "All right. The fifth."

interjections.text: Kessa, to nobody: "Sixty gold to send a man back to a town that won't feed him."
